Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 1:

﴿By the sky containing the burūj (constellations)﴾: the stars, twelve burūj (constellations, star mansions), which were mentioned earlier in Surah al-Furqan.
﴿And by the Promised Day﴾ — the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 3:

﴿And the witness﴾ is the Day of Jumu'ah (Friday), ﴿and the witnessed﴾ is the Day of 'Arafah; thus were the three explained in the hadith. The first is the one promised, the second is the one who witnesses by the deed performed on it, and the third is the one witnessed by the people and the angels. The answer to the oath is omitted, its beginning being, its estimated sense being: "Indeed..." (laqad).

Translation of the passage:

﴿Qutila﴾ (was cursed) ﴿the companions of the trench﴾ (al-ukhdud), meaning the ditch dug in the earth.
﴿The fire﴾ is a *badal ishtimal* (a substitution of inclusion, where the substituted noun contains or encompasses what it replaces) from it. ﴿Full of fuel﴾: that with which it is kindled.
﴿When they were sitting around it﴾: around it, on the edge of the trench, on the seats, sitting.

Translation of the commentary:

﴿And they, over what they were doing to the believers﴾ — [i.e., the disbelievers, over their torturing of the believers] by casting them into the fire, if they did not turn back from their faith, ﴿were witnesses﴾ — present (ḥuḍūr). It is related that God saved the believers who were cast into the fire by taking their souls before they fell into it, and the fire came out upon those who were there and burned them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 8:

﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾, the One who is praised.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 9:

﴿Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.﴾ Meaning: the disbelievers did not object to the believers except for their faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women﴾ by burning them, ﴿and then did not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell﴾ because of their disbelief, ﴿and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾, i.e., the punishment for their burning of the believers in the Hereafter. It was also said that it refers to this world, by a fire being brought out and burning them, as was mentioned earlier.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 12:

﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord﴾ upon the disbelievers ﴿is severe﴾ according to His will.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 13:

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates [the creation]﴾ [i.e., the creation] ﴿and repeats [it]﴾, so nothing He wills is beyond His power.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 14:**

﴿And He is the Forgiving﴾ to the sinning believers. [Al-Wadud (the Loving)] ﴿the One who shows affection to His friends (awliya') through honor﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 15:

﴿Possessor of the Throne﴾, its Creator and its Owner; ﴿the Glorious﴾ — with a raised (ḍamma) vowel, i.e., the one deserving of the perfection of the attributes of Exaltedness.

The commentary on Surah 85, verse 16:

﴿Fa'‘āluń limā yurīd﴾ (Mighty doer of whatever He wills): nothing can overpower Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 85, verse 17:

﴿Has there come to you﴾ O Muhammad, "the story of the armies"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 18:

﴿Pharaoh and Thamud﴾ is in apposition (badal) to "the hosts," and by mentioning Pharaoh, his followers are dispensed with. And the account (hadith) of them is that they were destroyed for their disbelief. And this is a warning to those who disbelieve in the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, so that they may take heed.
﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve are in denial﴾ of what has been mentioned.
﴿And Allah is encompassing them from behind them﴾, so there is no protector for them from Him.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 85, verse 21:**

﴿Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾ , magnificent.

Translation:

﴿In a Preserved Tablet﴾ — it is in the air above the seventh heaven, ﴿preserved﴾ from the devils by being kept away from them, and from any alteration to any part of it. Its length is the distance between heaven and earth, and its width is the distance between east and west. It is a white pearl; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.
